result.title: Coverage Cliffs in Off-Policy Quantile Certification
result.summary: We study when logged contextual-bandit data can certify an upper tail quantile for a policy selected from the same sample. We construct a PAC-Bayes Bernstein lower-confidence envelope for the target cumulative distribution function (CDF), simultaneous over a predeclared threshold grid and all data-dependent posteriors. The resulting procedure, TailCert, uses the envelope's first crossing of level p to return an atom-safe upper confidence bound on the selected posterior's pooled p-quantile (or inconclusive). It can also be used to select a policy under a certified tail constraint. The concentration ingredients are standard; the main theoretical contribution is a matched finite-class certification boundary comparing full logs with their joint weighted CDF indicators at a fixed threshold. On an explicit rare-action class, the required sample size grows linearly with the overlap factor W, logarithmically with policy-search and confidence complexity, and quadratically with the inverse CDF safety margin; the upper and lower bounds agree up to constants in the stated regime. On this class, the CDF reduction hides which actions exceeded the budget; retaining action counts restores the full-log rate. Simulations verify the predicted search-complexity shift, winner's-curse failure of naive reuse, and the power cost of splitting.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究用同一样本选出的策略能否凭日志数据认证其尾部上分位数，提出 TailCert：在阈值网格与所有数据相关后验上同时成立的 PAC-Bayes 下置信包络，以及匹配的有限类认证边界，并给出稀有动作类上样本量随覆盖因子、搜索复杂度与安全裕度的增长规律。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心结论「把完整日志压成 CDF 指示量会丢失动作身份并改变样本复杂度速率」可能为核查 latent 状态是否保留任务必要信息、压缩造成的速率退化提供类比线索；认证失败时返回 inconclusive 也可供核查带保证的停止决策。
